# Sahasra Electronic Solutions Limited SME Research

Information cutoff20October2026 · Official price19October2026 · NSE Emerge SME · INR crore unless stated · Master Prompt v3.0

## 1. Executive Verdict

**Hold, unresolved. Not investment-eligible and not a compounder designation.** Sahasra Electronic Solutions Limited has a real EMS business and a rapidly ramping semiconductor-packaging subsidiary, but the evidence does not yet establish reliable inventory economics, repeatable cash conversion or a fully funded growth path. At the official 19 October 2026 close of ₹420.05, a recovery narrative is already expensive relative to FY26 operating earnings. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS rather than false precision; the populated factors and exact uncertainty bounds are shown below. This is a research classification, not a statement that the issuer is in default. [AR26, E02–E10]

The favorable case is concrete: parent sales recovered to ₹123.6136 crore, FY26 consolidated operating EBITDA excluding other income rose to ₹18.1577 crore, and management's provisional Q1FY27 semiconductor sales almost equaled that subsidiary's entire FY26 revenue. Existing EMS customer qualifications, exports and installed assets make further growth possible. The unfavorable evidence is equally concrete: FY26 operating cash flow was negative ₹10.1322 crore despite a large cash subsidy received in the year; inventory and receivables absorbed cash; the notes disclose a missing quantitative stock reconciliation and post-year-end SAP mismatch correction. The auditor's unmodified opinions and improved edit logs are meaningful counterevidence, not proof that these economic questions are closed. [AR26 printed 133–138 and 169; BUS_Q1FY27; E03, E07]

The conclusion turns on **cash-backed, independently reconciled production and collections**, not on whether India needs more electronics manufacturing. A conditional five-year bullish funding experiment is provided, not a price target. It requires material hypothetical financing, favorable working-capital normalization and minority-value assumptions. Even then, its central earned-ROIC terminal outcome is substantially below the starting price; its identical ten-year extension fails an intraperiod cash test. There is no ordinary shareholder return printed for any failed path. No unsupported merger earnings, unapproved capital issue, restricted IPO deposit or pre-entry dividend is used to improve returns.

## 4. Business Overview

SESL manufactures printed-circuit-board assemblies, wire harnesses, box builds, memory modules and devices, and selected IT hardware. It earns manufacturing and integration revenue rather than software subscription revenue. SSPL performs semiconductor assembly, testing, marking and packaging; it is not a front-end silicon wafer foundry. The product descriptions matter because capital intensity, inventory obsolescence, qualification barriers and achievable margins differ sharply across these activities. [BUS_AR26 printed 11–18; BUS_PRES26]

The operating model combines customer design/qualification requirements with material procurement, assembly, testing and delivery. Imported electronic components and export receivables create working-capital and currency exposure. Management describes approximately 90% repeat customers, but most contracts are up to one year, so repeat business is not a contractual annuity. Customer qualification and switching effort can sustain relationships; customer ownership of designs, competitive tendering and component pass-through can limit pricing power. The report therefore separates repeat-order potential from legally committed backlog. [BUS_CALL26; BUS_AR26]

Related-party channels are economically significant: FY26 sales to Optima Technology Associates were ₹33.4322 crore, about 24.1% of consolidated revenue. That is a concentration and collection issue to examine, not evidence that the sales are fictitious. Management's FY26 product-mix bridge shows EMS ₹91.6 crore, memory ₹26.3 crore, IT ₹5.2 crore and semiconductor ₹15.7 crore; the audited note 27 classifications differ materially. They are not interchangeable segment accounts. Audited annual exports were ₹78.5995 crore, about 56.6%, whereas a deck used 55.8%. The audited denominator is used for annual exposure; provisional Q1 mix is kept separate. [AR26 notes 27 and 49; PRESENTATION26 PDF7; financial_inputs.presentation_reconciliations]

The four economic peers are Syrma SGS, Avalon Technologies, Cyient DLM and DCX Systems. Their comparison concerns manufacturing mix, working capital and returns, not a mechanical valuation median. Large-scale EMS diversification and defense/aerospace qualification are not attributes automatically transferable to Sahasra. No cutoff-date peer price multiple is manufactured where matching share and claim data were not established.

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

A moderate moat is more defensible than either a commodity-only dismissal or a semiconductor-premium claim. Long-lived EMS qualifications, export execution and test capabilities can make switching inconvenient. Packaging production requires process yield, reliability and customer approvals, so installed lines can create an opportunity. However, disclosed orders and equipment alone do not demonstrate scarcity rents, proprietary technology, durable pricing power or high returns on the full capital base. Most revenue remains outside the emerging packaging opportunity. MOAT is 5 with Medium confidence. [BUS_AR26; BUS_CALL26; E05]

Economic evidence constrains the narrative. FY26 operating EBITDA margin excluding other income is about 13.1%, below the exceptional parent FY24 margin. The parent recovery and SSPL scale-up coexist with ₹49.421 crore inventory and ₹43.665 crore receivables. The related Optima channel adds commercial access but concentration. Product-price inflation can increase gross revenue without proportional value addition, and memory pricing makes a revenue-only growth claim less secure. Inventory age, yield/scrap, customer-program profitability, replacement cycles and contractual pass-through mechanisms remain the next useful evidence, not a generic industry TAM. [AR26 notes 10, 12, 27 and 49]

Primary peer evidence shows that scale does not eliminate funding risk. Syrma's FY26 operating margin was about 11.3% and Avalon about 10.8%, both with positive CFO. Cyient DLM's revenue declined even though cash conversion improved; DCX's revenue and operating profitability fell while inventory and investment demands remained high. Definitions of net working-capital days and capital expenditure differ, so raw company ratios are not ranked as if identical. This cross-check makes a 20% sustained Sahasra bullish margin an optimistic assumption requiring proof, not an industry norm. The market snapshot and historical multiple cross-checks below use the official close and current issued shares, not the proposed merger denominator. The principal valuation is a monthly, event-ordered cash and claims experiment from 31 March 2026 through 19 October entry and then five or ten years. The seven-period pre-entry bridge is an **unobserved counterfactual**, not actual interim accounts. Bear/base/bull revenue growth is 3%/20%/30%, operating EBITDA margin 8%/16%/20%, DSO 150/115/90, with distinct inventory, other-operating-asset, supplier and customer-advance ratios. All five working-capital stocks roll forward. Routine obligations, positive WC investment and capex precede a front-loaded cash-cost event; revenue/cost remainder and negative-WC release follow. This exposes funding gaps hidden by annual positive cash. Opening tax, accrued interest, other obligations, dividend and employee provisions are tracked separately, not omitted in a net-debt shortcut. [model_inputs; model_spec]

Cash pools are legally differentiated: IPO deposits mature into IPO cash only, and pay modeled original-object eligible capex and residual issue expenses; margin deposits never become usable. Free-deposit availability has a zero-release sensitivity. Normalized cash taxes use positive operating EBIT less cash interest and quarterly payments, with no assumed cash tax benefit on losses. Existing term and lease principal amortize, PCFC must be repaid at an explicitly assumed maturity unless a separately labeled same-cap renewal is enabled, and renewals create no cash. There is no approved new placement or debt commitment in this evidence set. For surviving paths, terminal ROIC is the lower of the stated mature target and actually modeled terminal NOPAT divided by committed operating capital. Productive-capital reinvestment is next-year NOPAT × g / earned ROIC. Because the necessary operating-cash stock is excluded from productive IC, the increase from current to next-year required operating cash is separately deducted from FCFF; growth in that cash reserve is not free. A terminal growth rate at or above earned ROIC, or WACC at or below growth, cannot support the perpetuity. WACC 14–18% and g 2–5% are tested separately from 12/15/18% shareholder hurdles. The ordinary value bridge is claim-neutral: retain the operating/tax/interest reserve, add cash above that nonprincipal reserve, subtract all debt/leases and unpaid legacy financial claims once, then apply a stated residual-group-equity NCI proxy. The required principal reserve still constrains terminal funding, but is not deducted again from cash when the same debt is subtracted in the value bridge. The proxy 10% is tested at 5%, 15% and 27.3%; it is not falsely called the 27.3% subsidiary ownership percentage applied mechanically to the whole group.

The reserve includes one month cash operating cost, next-year principal, unpaid tax and next month's interest. The full reserve is a funding-adequacy test. In ordinary valuation, cash earmarked for principal is matched against that debt only once. A separately labeled conservative reserve-stress diagnostic may retain the principal reserve and also deduct debt, but it is not the ordinary intrinsic-value or return basis. A reserve gap blocks ordinary terminal price, IRR, hurdle and P/E returns even when the preceding horizon has no negative cash event. The original ₹40 crore gross-equity bull has a ₹10.5181 crore gap and is therefore not a funded terminal. A separately labeled ₹55 crore gross-equity experiment uses the same dates, issue price, fees, two-million-share limit and hypothetical expanded authorization to test a genuinely covered terminal reserve. This is extra conditional financing, not a retroactive cure or an actual placement. All ordinary WACC/g, minority, hurdle and reverse calculations use the same claim-neutral cash/debt convention and fund growth in operating cash. Dividends paid before the entry date reduce company cash but never appear as returns to the new investor; post-entry dividends are zero in these experiments. Retained FCFF is not simultaneously paid out and added to terminal cash.

Current-price preservation, 15% hurdle achievement and 5×/10× outcomes are searched on the declared finite grid without assuming monotonicity: higher growth can fail because of working capital. A failure to find a feasible point is a bounded negative result, not a mathematical proof over every possible future. R and P remain NS. The favorable central model result is not a supported buy price, particularly given G2/G3 and the terminal reserve gap.

Monthly/annual fcff is explicitly a subtotal before the separately shown opening operating-claim and employee-benefit cash settlements. ## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

The strongest bear case is a connected cash-and-control mechanism rather than “competition” in the abstract. Suppose the packaging ramp requires inventory before collections; component costs or yields deteriorate; long-dated and related-channel receivables are slow; tax credits and grants do not turn into freely available cash; and an assumed PCFC renewal or capex reallocation is unavailable. Restricted IPO cash cannot pay ordinary creditors. Debt service, tax and employee/customer commitments then consume the genuinely free pool before reported annual profit translates into cash. Forced financing can dilute shareholders or delay projects precisely when execution is weakest. [AR26; CARE monitoring; E03, E06–E10]

If inventories require write-downs or related receivables are impaired, the same shock reduces net assets, profit, borrowing availability and terminal cash generation. This is why downside cannot be estimated by applying a lower P/E to unadjusted owner PAT alone. Specialized assets, partly installed packaging equipment, export obligations and entity-level minority claims make liquidation recovery uncertain. No unsupported book-value floor or zero-loss cash balance is offered. D stays NS; illustrative customs and ring-fence stresses are not legal claim valuations or allegations of insolvency.

Counterevidence is material: no lender default or fraud was reported by the FY26 auditor, cash subsidy arrived, specified IPO shortfalls were restored, assets and customer relationships exist, and management has announced strong provisional Q1 sales. A purely pessimistic forecast would ignore these. The model therefore retains favorable funding and collection combinations alongside the failed ones. Nevertheless, **the thesis-break variable is verified unrestricted cash after inventory/receivable investment and scheduled claims**, supported by a signed stock bridge. An increasing sales number without that evidence does not falsify the bear case.

The monthly failures are conditional consequences of selected assumptions, including unobserved pre-entry cash flows and assumed debt dates. They are never described as actual historical defaults. Once a modeled path fails, ordinary IRR, terminal equity and hurdle entry are suppressed for the entire path, even if later cash is positive. A terminal reserve gap is a separate funding failure that also suppresses ordinary proceeds. No automatic unsecured overdraft or unbounded emergency equity is added. Sources do not all provide the same assurance. Audited accounts give verified reported values but do not eliminate disclosed reconciliation weaknesses. CARE cash restoration is not shareholder authorization. A management presentation's capacity, order book or provisional sales is not audited operating cash flow. An exchange announcement index confirms what was located in its scope, not that an unlocated approval can never exist. An authored calculation is reproducible, but its economic confidence cannot exceed the material inputs. Unknown current restrictions, live depth, order terms, exact customs exposure, project-level returns and target-company eliminations are explicitly retained.

The principal open questions are whether stock and receivables reconcile to cash, whether IPO and related-party governance remediation is complete, how much group cash is legally usable at each entity, when borrowings mature and can be renewed, whether the recent packaging ramp earns adequate returns after full capital needs, and what the effective merger would do to each shareholder's economic interest. Until these are answered, a supported base IRR, normalized owner-PAT forecast and ordinary investment score remain NS.

The reproducible record separates authored inputs from generated outputs. Its aggregate authored-input fingerprint binds an ordered list of input names and SHA256 values; it is **not the SHA256 file hash of the report or reader record**. Those file hashes are separately attested after generation. The recovery test starts with every generated output and attestation poisoned or deleted, disallows network and subprocess use, permits only declared authored input reads or outputs written during that run, and performs verification inside those guards. This protects reproducibility, not the truth of a management forecast. Research update: first full v3.0 assessment at the stated cutoff; no prior company score is silently overwritten.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown:
**Hold, unresolved. Not investment-eligible and not a compounder designation.** Sahasra Electronic Solutions Limited has a real EMS business and a rapidly ramping semiconductor-packaging subsidiary, but the evidence does not yet establish reliable inventory economics, repeatable cash conversion or a fully funded growth path. At the official 19 October 2026 close of ₹420.05, a recovery narrative is already expensive relative to FY26 operating earnings. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS rather than false precision; the populated factors and exact uncertainty bounds are shown below. This is a research classification, not a statement that the issuer is in default. [AR26, E02–E10]

The favorable case is concrete: parent sales recovered to ₹123.6136 crore, FY26 consolidated operating EBITDA excluding other income rose to ₹18.1577 crore, and management's provisional Q1FY27 semiconductor sales almost equaled that subsidiary's entire FY26 revenue. Existing EMS customer qualifications, exports and installed assets make further growth possible. The unfavorable evidence is equally concrete: FY26 operating cash flow was negative ₹10.1322 crore despite a large cash subsidy received in the year; inventory and receivables absorbed cash; the notes disclose a missing quantitative stock reconciliation and post-year-end SAP mismatch correction. The auditor's unmodified opinions and improved edit logs are meaningful counterevidence, not proof that these economic questions are closed. [AR26 printed 133–138 and 169; BUS_Q1FY27; E03, E07]

The conclusion turns on **cash-backed, independently reconciled production and collections**, not on whether India needs more electronics manufacturing. A conditional five-year bullish funding experiment is provided, not a price target. It requires material hypothetical financing, favorable working-capital normalization and minority-value assumptions. Even then, its central earned-ROIC terminal outcome is substantially below the starting price; its identical ten-year extension fails an intraperiod cash test. There is no ordinary shareholder return printed for any failed path. No unsupported merger earnings, unapproved capital issue, restricted IPO deposit or pre-entry dividend is used to improve returns.

It earns manufacturing and integration revenue rather than software subscription revenue. The product descriptions matter because capital intensity, inventory obsolescence, qualification barriers and achievable margins differ sharply across these activities. [BUS_AR26 printed 11–18; BUS_PRES26]

The operating model combines customer design/qualification requirements with material procurement, assembly, testing and delivery. Imported electronic components and export receivables create working-capital and currency exposure. Management describes approximately 90% repeat customers, but most contracts are up to one year, so repeat business is not a contractual annuity. Customer qualification and switching effort can sustain relationships; customer ownership of designs, competitive tendering and component pass-through can limit pricing power. The report therefore separates repeat-order potential from legally committed backlog. [BUS_CALL26; BUS_AR26]

Related-party channels are economically significant: FY26 sales to Optima Technology Associates were ₹33.4322 crore, about 24.1% of consolidated revenue. That is a concentration and collection issue to examine, not evidence that the sales are fictitious. Management's FY26 product-mix bridge shows EMS ₹91.6 crore, memory ₹26.3 crore, IT ₹5.2 crore and semiconductor ₹15.7 crore; the audited note 27 classifications differ materially. They are not interchangeable segment accounts. Audited annual exports were ₹78.5995 crore, about 56.6%, whereas a deck used 55.8%. The audited denominator is used for annual exposure; provisional Q1 mix is kept separate. [AR26 notes 27 and 49; PRESENTATION26 PDF7; financial_inputs.presentation_reconciliations]

The four economic peers are Syrma SGS, Avalon Technologies, Cyient DLM and DCX Systems. Their comparison concerns manufacturing mix, working capital and returns, not a mechanical valuation median. Large-scale EMS diversification and defense/aerospace qualification are not attributes automatically transferable to Sahasra. No cutoff-date peer price multiple is manufactured where matching share and claim data were not established.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
A moderate moat is more defensible than either a commodity-only dismissal or a semiconductor-premium claim. Long-lived EMS qualifications, export execution and test capabilities can make switching inconvenient. Packaging production requires process yield, reliability and customer approvals, so installed lines can create an opportunity. However, disclosed orders and equipment alone do not demonstrate scarcity rents, proprietary technology, durable pricing power or high returns on the full capital base. Most revenue remains outside the emerging packaging opportunity. MOAT is 5 with Medium confidence. [BUS_AR26; BUS_CALL26; E05]

Economic evidence constrains the narrative. FY26 operating EBITDA margin excluding other income is about 13.1%, below the exceptional parent FY24 margin. The parent recovery and SSPL scale-up coexist with ₹49.421 crore inventory and ₹43.665 crore receivables. The related Optima channel adds commercial access but concentration. Product-price inflation can increase gross revenue without proportional value addition, and memory pricing makes a revenue-only growth claim less secure. Inventory age, yield/scrap, customer-program profitability, replacement cycles and contractual pass-through mechanisms remain the next useful evidence, not a generic industry TAM. [AR26 notes 10, 12, 27 and 49]

Primary peer evidence shows that scale does not eliminate funding risk. Syrma's FY26 operating margin was about 11.3% and Avalon about 10.8%, both with positive CFO. Cyient DLM's revenue declined even though cash conversion improved; DCX's revenue and operating profitability fell while inventory and investment demands remained high. Definitions of net working-capital days and capital expenditure differ, so raw company ratios are not ranked as if identical. This cross-check makes a 20% sustained Sahasra bullish margin an optimistic assumption requiring proof, not an industry norm. sections.content_markdown:
The historical table deliberately preserves predecessor, short-period successor, standalone, first consolidated and later comparative vintages. Company FY23 was only 38 days; its percentage growth into FY24 is a base distortion and not used as the business growth score. FY25 group growth is not comparable with FY24 parent alone because the subsidiary entered consolidation. FY26 group revenue grew from ₹95.8475 crore to ₹138.7677 crore, while parent revenue grew from ₹86.8267 crore to ₹123.6136 crore. The parent has therefore recovered strongly, but FY25's decline from ₹101.1528 crore remains visible. [DRHP; AR25; AR26]

Management's product bridge attributes about ₹43 crore FY26 growth to EMS +₹31.1 crore, memory +₹13.8 crore, IT −₹8.4 crore and packaging +₹6.5 crore. This is useful directional attribution, not an audited constant-classification volume/price/acquisition reconciliation. Packaging's prior-year consolidation commenced after 21 June 2024; an unchanged twelve-month perimeter is not established. Memory prices, shipment units, customer wins versus existing programs and intra-group eliminations are ND. Organic group CAGR is therefore NS even though reported revenue and the separately declared parent continuity CAGR can be calculated. The latter is diagnostic, not a scored organic-demand measure. [PRESENTATION26 PDF7; AR25 note58; E11]

The July/September provisional Q1FY27 update reports group sales ₹47.90 crore versus ₹22.03 crore, parent ₹32.96 crore versus ₹20.42 crore and SSPL ₹14.94 crore. That is a notable ramp, especially against SSPL's roughly ₹15.69 crore FY26, but one quarter cannot establish annual repeatability, collections or unit economics. The reported ₹7.29 crore EBITDA label alongside ₹2.32 crore other income is not treated as a verified operating-margin bridge. No Q1 CFO is inferred from earnings. [BUS_Q1FY27; BUS_SEP_DECK]

Combining them mechanically with Q1 sales gives ₹140.9 crore versus the same presentation's existing-perimeter ₹200 crore FY27 target, leaving ₹59.1 crore uncovered even before order timing, cancellations and double-counting checks. sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
Packaging and electronics localization provide plausible addressable demand, but investment attractiveness requires a funded route to acceptable incremental returns. Management's roadmap places microSD, eSIM, LED drivers and RFID in production across October 2024 to January 2026. eMMC/eSSD mass production planned for Q4 2027 and advanced packaging in 2028 or later are future milestones, not current earnings. Suggested ₹200 crore semiconductor expansion plus ₹50 crore R&D is not added to the base as funded growth. UltraMax Sahasra Energy is a separate 60:40 promoter venture, explicitly outside SESL; no value is assigned without a transaction and minority-fairness analysis. [BUS_SEP_DECK; BUS_CALL26]

Capacity claims need reconciliation. May materials described Noida peak revenue capacity ₹100 crore and Bhiwadi ₹200 crore; September raised Bhiwadi to ₹400 crore while repeating a 22.5% utilization label that corresponds to ₹44.9/₹200 crore, not ₹44.9/₹400 crore. A four-plus-eight versus four-plus-four SMT-line inconsistency also remains. These were checked in the original rendered presentation pages rather than dismissed as OCR errors. Thus capacity is not simply multiplied by an assumed utilization rate to manufacture revenue. Machine availability, bottleneck yield, qualification, shifts, component supply and cash funding all matter. [BUS_PRES26; BUS_SEP_DECK PDF36–37; E12]

The capital bridge below computes operating invested capital on both asset and financing bases, retaining goodwill, ROU/CWIP, capital advances and minority capital. FY26 normalized NOPAT divided by average capital is only about 3.0%; the one-year incremental proxy is about 10.7%, below the 14–18% WACC range. Neither is a mature project IRR. Depreciation, grant accounting, cash capex versus additions, the ₹2.4761 crore GST reclassification and operating-asset movements leave an explicitly unclosed bridge residual. With a short group history and inventory reliability questions, CAP stays NS instead of scoring a superficially precise incremental return. [AR26 notes 3, 4, 10–13, 38 and 54; E09]

Cash conversion constrains durability. The parent three-year ratio of summed CFO to summed PAT is negative; group two-year CFO is also negative despite total PAT turning positive. Capex does not explain weak CFO because investing cash outflows occur below CFO. Management's expectation of consolidated positive CFO only by end-FY28 is a caution about the funding interval, not a reason to waive it. GQS is NS with its bounds capped at 5 because CASH is 3. A growing order book cannot neutralize this override. [AR25; AR26; CALL26]

The model carries a further ₹1.5437 crore of noncash operating assets: ₹1.4430 crore noncurrent security/other operating deposits, ₹0.0714 crore other noncurrent assets beyond capital advances and ₹0.0293 crore other current financial assets beyond deposits/interest. It assumes no release or depreciation and includes them in terminal IC. Model opening gross operating IC of ₹249.5906 crore less ₹3.4650 crore separately modeled opening operating cash claims reconciles to audited asset-side operating IC of ₹246.1256 crore. This distinction prevents settling those claims in cash while also pretending their opening financing benefit persists forever. [AR26 printed131–132, notes4,6,11,18,23–24]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.content_markdown:
Promoters held 17,469,500 shares, approximately 69.90%, at 31 March 2026. The resulting 7,523,263 non-promoter shares are an upper bound on float, not verified continuously tradable free float. The April encumbrance declaration says no other encumbrance was made during the financial year; it is not a blanket independent assertion of zero current pledges at the cutoff. Directors' FY26 remuneration of ₹1.98 crore to Amrit Lal Manwani, ₹1.122 crore to Varun Manwani and ₹0.396 crore to Arunima Manwani totals ₹3.498 crore and is assessed against the group's earnings and cash, without alleging impropriety merely because family members are involved. [AR26 note49; pledge26; security_inputs]

The original FY25 CARO reported non-object IPO deployments including ₹4.60 crore to Infopower and ₹14.40 crore subsidiary equity, an almost-year-long inactive edit trail, and the need to strengthen internal audit. Later monitoring gives important remediation: the parent ₹3.52 crore matured-FD usage was restored by Q4FY26; the subsidiary ₹2.85 crore cash shortfall was restored in Q1/Q2, and its original ₹22.92 crore capex was completed on 29 August 2025 after a 151-day delay. A board resolution supporting FD parking was received. These are genuine resolutions, not omitted counterevidence. [AR25 CARO; audit_history CARE chronology]

Separately, a ₹2.68 crore subsidiary material deviation still lacked shareholder approval in the June 2026 monitoring record. A NIL-new-deviation headline does not close that older item. The 4 July board proposal to reallocate ₹40 crore from parent capex to subsidiary capex was subject to shareholder approval. The reviewed 3 August AGM agenda and proceedings did not establish specific approval or ratification; its related-party resolution is not treated as a substitute. The model therefore never presumes that the reallocation became lawful or available. These approval and proceeds-tracing questions justify G1 hold and GOV 4, not an unsupported fraud finding. [dividend26; audit_history AGM and CARE sources]

FY26 unmodified financial and IFC opinions, preserved audit logs and no reported fraud, lender default, wilful-default designation or auditor resignation are favorable developments. The earlier statutory auditor's voluntary resignation is retained in the history, rather than described as continuing in FY26. The July results clarification corrected a missing comparative and an EPS/XBRL error, not a demonstrated wholesale earnings restatement. Against that, absent inventory reconciliation and pending counterparty confirmations require auditor-level closure. Management says SAP S/4HANA went live on 1 September 2026; a new system alone does not prove old inventory balances were correct. [AR26 audits/CARO; audit_history; BUS_SEP_DECK]

The pending common-control merger adds governance complexity. Corrected exchange ratios are 226 SESL shares per 100 SEPL shares, 5 per 100 Infopower shares and 55 per 100 SSSDPL shares. The correction's total 29,975,408 differs by one share from its stated promoter-plus-public sum. It is a proposed denominator, not current shares. Common-control pooling, related-party fairness, loans eliminated and transferor debt/cash must be reconciled before valuing the combined entity. The scheme's ₹287.69 SESL value based on a March VWAP rule is not an October fair-value conclusion. [SCHEME; SWAP_CORRECTION; VALUATION_SCHEME]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.content_markdown:
**Earnings are improving, but owner profit, group profit and operating profit are different numbers.** FY26 group PAT was ₹12.1289 crore; loss allocated to NCI was ₹2.0596 crore, leaving owner PAT ₹14.1885 crore. FY25 group PAT was negative ₹2.3439 crore while owner PAT remained positive ₹2.8016 crore because NCI absorbed ₹5.1455 crore of loss. Group CFO must therefore not be divided by owner PAT without acknowledging the scope mismatch. Annual FY26 EPS of ₹5.68 agrees with owner profit and 24,992,763 weighted shares; parent EPS ₹7.87 is not a consolidated denominator. [AR26 printed 133–138, note37]

Operating EBIT excludes all ₹9.6485 crore other income: interest ₹5.2538 crore, grant amortization ₹2.8964 crore, liability write-back ₹0.2052 crore, rebates ₹0.1332 crore and miscellaneous ₹1.1599 crore. PBT plus finance cost less other income gives operating EBIT ₹8.7371 crore; adding depreciation ₹9.4206 crore gives EBITDA ₹18.1577 crore. The reported-including-other-income EBITDA is ₹27.8062 crore and is shown separately, not used to support manufacturing economics. A normalized 25% operating tax yields NOPAT ₹6.552825 crore. No arbitrary normalized owner PAT is invented because entity-level tax, minority allocation and subsidy treatment are unresolved. DTA/MAT accounting benefits are not future cash. [AR26 notes 28, 33 and 37; E02]

FY26 CFO starts from reported pre-working-capital cash profit ₹19.6596 crore. Receivables consumed ₹17.7250 crore, inventory ₹11.4670 crore, other operating assets ₹20.3622 crore and other financial assets ₹2.9941 crore; changes in liabilities partly offset these. The full reconciliation is below. The cash-flow statement's tax line is positive ₹1.8159 crore; it is retained as reported without inventing documentary proof of a tax refund. Interest paid ₹4.2701 crore is classified in financing, so an interest-normalized CFO cross-check is negative ₹14.4023 crore. Cash capex ₹9.0761 crore then leaves reported CFO-minus-capex negative ₹19.2083 crore. [AR26 printed137–138]

A ₹21.8853034 crore capital subsidy was received by year end. The disbursement letter's final ₹18.6025080 crore installment was verified visually, correcting misleading OCR. Deferred grant ₹18.9889 crore is not debt. The cash-flow statement does not isolate the receipt, so subtracting the subsidy from CFO gives only a conditional diagnostic of negative ₹32.0175034 crore if it is included there, not an asserted corrected audit cash flow. Neither that receipt nor ₹2.8964 crore grant amortization is projected as annual recurring cash. [SUBSIDY p1; AR26 grant and CF notes]

Cash availability is more restrictive than the headline. ₹23.4512 crore cash includes ₹6.36 crore IPO cash. ₹44.7803 crore current deposits include an inferred ₹40.50 crore IPO balance, leaving only ₹4.2803 crore as an upper-bound non-IPO deposit pool; bank/entity mapping is not proven. ₹9.5255 crore long deposits are margin/security and unavailable. Non-IPO cash ₹17.0912 crore is substantially at the subsidiary and not automatically fungible. Borrowing carrying value ₹66.4813 crore differs from gross scheduled principal ₹66.5930 crore because of fees; PCFC ₹29.7434 crore, term current ₹9.4963 crore, leases, tax, accrued interest and other claims are modeled separately. Capital commitment ₹13.1356 crore is a subset of planned capex, not another copy of the cash outflow. [AR26 notes 9, 11, 16–26; CARE monitor]

The receivable ageing includes ₹6.2405 crore older than one year and ₹1.8676 crore beyond three years, alongside a separately impaired disputed ₹0.1465 crore. Confirmations remain pending. Optima receivables ₹7.108 crore, Rwanda ₹3.3424 crore and proprietor ₹1.2448 crore merit collection evidence. Infopower's ₹6.60 crore loan and ₹0.7812 crore interest are not counted as cash; CARO notes no fixed repayment terms and interest not received. Parent loans ₹30.55 crore and guarantee ₹27.50 crore to SSPL are already inside consolidated exposure and are not added again as group debt. [AR26 notes12,44,49 and CARO]

Comparative differences are preserved, not silently repaired: FY24 original AS PAT/CFO ₹33.2415/₹5.5412 crore, IPO-restated ₹32.6277/₹0.9466 crore and later Ind AS comparative ₹33.2423/₹5.1693 crore. FY25 group's FY26 comparative assets, receivables and payables are lower than the original report by approximately ₹1.0203 crore while equity, debt, P&L and CFO remain unchanged; netting is a possible explanation, not verified. Land/ROU, prior depreciation and GST reclassifications are listed in the capital bridge. Interim EPS also has unresolved numerator inconsistencies: H1FY25 comparative ₹2.15 aligns more closely with owner comprehensive income than owner PAT, and H1FY26 ₹1.68 similarly differs from the approximately ₹1.69 owner-PAT calculation. Annual EPS is not assumed wrong by association. [historical_inputs; audit_history; H1FY26; E11]

G2 remains a hold because an unmodified audit and clean IFC opinion coexist with the explicit note that quantitative raw-material/finished-goods reconciliation was not prepared, with SAP mismatches at 31 March reportedly rectified through 8 May. This requires a signed opening-purchases-consumption-closing bridge, stock valuation/yield support and auditor closure. No deliberate manipulation is inferred. Quantified contingent items sum to ₹0.4409 crore; the customs export-obligation amount is unascertained, not zero. Separate model shocks of ₹5/₹15 crore are stress assumptions, not estimates of an assessed legal demand. [AR26 printed169 and contingent note]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.content_markdown:
The market snapshot and historical multiple cross-checks below use the official close and current issued shares, not the proposed merger denominator. Owner PAT supports the reported P/E cross-check; consolidated operating EBITDA uses a group EV bridge including NCI book capital and leases. Different cash policies produce a range rather than a spurious single precise enterprise multiple. IPO and margin deposits cannot both fund operating growth and be subtracted as free cash. Forward price/earnings forecasts remain conditional because the supported normalized owner-earnings base is NS. [capital_oct; NSE market extract; AR26]

The principal valuation is a monthly, event-ordered cash and claims experiment from 31 March 2026 through 19 October entry and then five or ten years. The seven-period pre-entry bridge is an **unobserved counterfactual**, not actual interim accounts. Bear/base/bull revenue growth is 3%/20%/30%, operating EBITDA margin 8%/16%/20%, DSO 150/115/90, with distinct inventory, other-operating-asset, supplier and customer-advance ratios. All five working-capital stocks roll forward. Routine obligations, positive WC investment and capex precede a front-loaded cash-cost event; revenue/cost remainder and negative-WC release follow. This exposes funding gaps hidden by annual positive cash. Opening tax, accrued interest, other obligations, dividend and employee provisions are tracked separately, not omitted in a net-debt shortcut. [model_inputs; model_spec]

Cash pools are legally differentiated: IPO deposits mature into IPO cash only, and pay modeled original-object eligible capex and residual issue expenses; margin deposits never become usable. Free-deposit availability has a zero-release sensitivity. Normalized cash taxes use positive operating EBIT less cash interest and quarterly payments, with no assumed cash tax benefit on losses. Existing term and lease principal amortize, PCFC must be repaid at an explicitly assumed maturity unless a separately labeled same-cap renewal is enabled, and renewals create no cash. A group ring-fence test limits opening free cash to ₹4 crore. Receivable recovery and customs shocks are separate assumptions. All dates and all failed trial paths are retained in the reproducibility files.

There is no approved new placement or debt commitment in this evidence set. Hypothetical new bank debt is capped at ₹20 crore on 19 November 2026, carries 12% interest, 1% upfront fee and bounded amortization. Hypothetical equity on 19 December prices at 75% of entry, pays 2% fees and floors issuance to whole shares. Under the verified 25 million authorization, only 7,237 additional shares fit. A distinct expanded-authorization case assumes approval to 32 million on 19 November and caps issuance at two million shares and ₹40 crore gross. A post-breach capital injection never retrospectively repairs the failure. These financing dates are assumptions, not recommendations or claims that offers exist. [AR26 capital; model_inputs]

For surviving paths, terminal ROIC is the lower of the stated mature target and actually modeled terminal NOPAT divided by committed operating capital. Productive-capital reinvestment is next-year NOPAT × g / earned ROIC. Because the necessary operating-cash stock is excluded from productive IC, the increase from current to next-year required operating cash is separately deducted from FCFF; growth in that cash reserve is not free. A terminal growth rate at or above earned ROIC, or WACC at or below growth, cannot support the perpetuity. WACC 14–18% and g 2–5% are tested separately from 12/15/18% shareholder hurdles. The ordinary value bridge is claim-neutral: retain the operating/tax/interest reserve, add cash above that nonprincipal reserve, subtract all debt/leases and unpaid legacy financial claims once, then apply a stated residual-group-equity NCI proxy. The required principal reserve still constrains terminal funding, but is not deducted again from cash when the same debt is subtracted in the value bridge. The proxy 10% is tested at 5%, 15% and 27.3%; it is not falsely called the 27.3% subsidiary ownership percentage applied mechanically to the whole group.

The reserve includes one month cash operating cost, next-year principal, unpaid tax and next month's interest. The full reserve is a funding-adequacy test. In ordinary valuation, cash earmarked for principal is matched against that debt only once. A separately labeled conservative reserve-stress diagnostic may retain the principal reserve and also deduct debt, but it is not the ordinary intrinsic-value or return basis. A reserve gap blocks ordinary terminal price, IRR, hurdle and P/E returns even when the preceding horizon has no negative cash event. The original ₹40 crore gross-equity bull has a ₹10.5181 crore gap and is therefore not a funded terminal. A separately labeled ₹55 crore gross-equity experiment uses the same dates, issue price, fees, two-million-share limit and hypothetical expanded authorization to test a genuinely covered terminal reserve. This is extra conditional financing, not a retroactive cure or an actual placement. All ordinary WACC/g, minority, hurdle and reverse calculations use the same claim-neutral cash/debt convention and fund growth in operating cash. Dividends paid before the entry date reduce company cash but never appear as returns to the new investor; post-entry dividends are zero in these experiments. Retained FCFF is not simultaneously paid out and added to terminal cash.

The two-way operating and valuation grids, reverse growth searches, normalized P/E checks and all failure statuses below show why a single target price is unwarranted. Current-price preservation, 15% hurdle achievement and 5×/10× outcomes are searched on the declared finite grid without assuming monotonicity: higher growth can fail because of working capital. A failure to find a feasible point is a bounded negative result, not a mathematical proof over every possible future. R and P remain NS. The favorable central model result is not a supported buy price, particularly given G2/G3 and the terminal reserve gap.

Monthly/annual fcff is explicitly a subtotal before the separately shown opening operating-claim and employee-benefit cash settlements. Those settlements are already paid in the complete cash ledger; the subtotal is not a distributable cash figure and is never separately discounted or credited to shareholders. Opening tax, interest and pre-entry dividend retain their distinct treatment. The annual export labels this column fcff_before_separate_operating_settlements.

The algebraic hurdle-entry values hold the financing price fixed. Since the model prices hypothetical equity at75%of entry, a lower purchase price can reduce proceeds under the two-million-share cap. Separate exact12/15/18%hurdle-price and₹50–500 coupled-price grid replays reprice that future equity and rerun every funding/reserve test. A low algebraic hurdle value is therefore not automatically a financeable entry or recommendation.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The strongest bear case is a connected cash-and-control mechanism rather than “competition” in the abstract. Suppose the packaging ramp requires inventory before collections; component costs or yields deteriorate; long-dated and related-channel receivables are slow; tax credits and grants do not turn into freely available cash; and an assumed PCFC renewal or capex reallocation is unavailable. Restricted IPO cash cannot pay ordinary creditors. Debt service, tax and employee/customer commitments then consume the genuinely free pool before reported annual profit translates into cash. Forced financing can dilute shareholders or delay projects precisely when execution is weakest. [AR26; CARE monitoring; E03, E06–E10]

If inventories require write-downs or related receivables are impaired, the same shock reduces net assets, profit, borrowing availability and terminal cash generation. This is why downside cannot be estimated by applying a lower P/E to unadjusted owner PAT alone. Specialized assets, partly installed packaging equipment, export obligations and entity-level minority claims make liquidation recovery uncertain. No unsupported book-value floor or zero-loss cash balance is offered. D stays NS; illustrative customs and ring-fence stresses are not legal claim valuations or allegations of insolvency.

Counterevidence is material: no lender default or fraud was reported by the FY26 auditor, cash subsidy arrived, specified IPO shortfalls were restored, assets and customer relationships exist, and management has announced strong provisional Q1 sales. A purely pessimistic forecast would ignore these. The model therefore retains favorable funding and collection combinations alongside the failed ones. Nevertheless, **the thesis-break variable is verified unrestricted cash after inventory/receivable investment and scheduled claims**, supported by a signed stock bridge. An increasing sales number without that evidence does not falsify the bear case.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.content_markdown:
At ₹420.05, a 5× price would be ₹2,100.25 and a 10× price ₹4,200.50 before any dividends. Over five years those require approximately 38.0% and 58.5% annual shareholder compounding; over ten years approximately 17.5% and 25.9%. Company revenue growth alone is not shareholder compounding: margins, reinvestment, financing fees, dilution, NCI, retained cash and exit economics all intervene. The model tests both horizons with the same opening commitments and bounded finance, rather than making financing magically easier at ten years.

The finite reverse search varies revenue CAGR from 0% through 100% in five-percentage-point steps for the bullish operating ratios, without new finance, with the original ₹40 crore gross-equity package, and with a separately bounded ₹55 crore gross-equity package to test terminal reserve coverage. Every trial is retained, including negative-cash and unsustainable-terminal cases; the grid is not truncated at the first attractive outcome. A separate operating grid varies margin and DSO, because a revenue-only solution can be economically misleading. The target-capitalization and implied normalized PAT requirements at 10×/15×/20× P/E are shown below using both current and modeled diluted shares. These are necessary arithmetic burdens, not forecasts or assigned exit multiples.

An outcome is not labeled feasible merely because a terminal formula crosses 5× or 10× after a cash breach. Nor is a ten-year return printed because the ending balance is positive after a prior intraperiod deficit. The canonical path archive provides dates, finance caps, claims and earned reinvestment for every failed attempt. No observed evidence yet supports the sustained, cash-backed execution and minority economics needed for a multibagger designation. Even a finite-grid success, if any, remains an analyst experiment until funding, returns on incremental capital and the audit questions are resolved. [model_summary; trial_index; E14]

sections.content_markdown:
**First, close the accounting and funding evidence, not the price chart.** Obtain a signed quantitative inventory bridge by product, SAP cutover reconciliation, valuation/yield/scrap evidence and explicit auditor follow-up on the March mismatch; match receivable balances to subsequent collections and confirmations, especially Optima, Rwanda, the proprietor and Infopower. Reconcile FY24 AS/IPO/Ind AS cash-flow vintages, FY25 comparative balance netting and interim EPS numerators. A documented closure can improve G2; merely reporting higher sales cannot. [AR26 notes44,49,54,56; historical_inputs]

**Second, verify authority and cash access.** Obtain the full IPO proceeds ledger, bank-entity deposit restrictions/maturities, CARE follow-up and specific shareholder approval for the subsidiary deviation and any ₹40 crore object change. Confirm PCFC renewal/maturity, term amortization, covenants, FX exposure and capex commitments against signed sanction documents. Match current free cash and debt to the same date. A funded monthly plan must survive delayed customer collection, a lower margin and an unavailable deposit. This is the evidence needed to change G1/G3, not a pledge that the company must raise the modeled finance.

**Third, track delivery in comparable scope.** At each half-year and annual release, separate parent, subsidiary and any legally effective merger perimeter; reconcile units, prices, acquisitions and eliminations; show operating EBITDA excluding grants/interest, CFO before and after subsidy, inventory age and tax-credit realization. Confirm Q1 packaging sales convert into collections and orders recur. Check the promised FY27 subsidiary cash/EBITDA breakeven separately from PAT, and the FY28 consolidated CFO goal separately from capex-adjusted FCF. Capacity and SMT-line reconciliations should precede utilization-driven forecasts. [BUS_CALL26; BUS_SEP_DECK]

**Finally, re-underwrite the security.** Any merger approval, new capital authorization or issuance requires a refreshed share/debt/NCI bridge and price-implied return model. Update the 60-session turnover test, current lot, circuit band, surveillance and live depth before implementation. Warning triggers are renewed unreconciled inventory, persistent negative CFO despite reported profit, further non-object use without approval, material related-party collection slippage, funding unavailable before an obligation, or guidance increases unsupported by comparable orders and cash. These are monitoring conditions, not allegations that each has occurred.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
The formal outcome is **Hold — unresolved / pending evidence**, with Low overall confidence and BQS/GQS/IAS NS. It is not a ranked eligible idea, a recommended allocation, an evidenced compounder, an actual-default call or a conviction short. The complete classification matrix is not bypassed by substituting the best conditional scenario for a missing score. Parent-level historical growth, legitimate customer qualifications and packaging opportunity remain research positives, but they do not override G1/G2/G3 holds. The current price does not supply a demonstrated margin of safety against the unresolved capital and cash burden.

A conditional re-entry to investment analysis requires documentary closure of the inventory and comparative-account issues, authority and tracing for prior IPO deviations, same-date unrestricted cash/debt evidence and a realistically funded path through working-capital and capex needs. REV/CAP/BAL/R/D/P can then be rescored using the same fixed weights, with renewed downside and minority analysis. Even if those gates improve, a price or earnings change must still clear the chosen shareholder hurdle; accounting closure alone is not a buy signal.

The current 400-share lot makes even a small reference position lumpy. The ₹5 lakh liquidity test is a research convention, not a suggestion to buy three lots or commit any amount. This dossier does not execute trades, publish a site, or alter a portfolio. It provides a reproducible SME record in the existing research format, to be considered separately from the main-board universe and not silently merged into a ranked list while NS fields remain.

Primary issuer and NSE records underpin material historical claims: original annual financials and audit/CARO/IFC reports, IPO restated statements, monitoring reports, AGM/resolution documents, the scheme/correction and valuation annexure, original results and presentations, capital certificate, dated security master and sixty exchange-session records. The evidence ledger links each material conclusion to a source and locator, distinguishes V/C/M/A, and records contradictions. Public source URLs and hashes identify retrieved originals; local raw PDFs/OCR, private identifiers, transfer credentials and internal coordination are excluded from the recovery artifacts. Peer economic figures come from named official company disclosures, with differing definitions preserved. [source_map; evidence_ledger; audit_history; business_sources; peer_inputs]

Sources do not all provide the same assurance. Audited accounts give verified reported values but do not eliminate disclosed reconciliation weaknesses. CARE cash restoration is not shareholder authorization. A management presentation's capacity, order book or provisional sales is not audited operating cash flow. An exchange announcement index confirms what was located in its scope, not that an unlocated approval can never exist. An authored calculation is reproducible, but its economic confidence cannot exceed the material inputs. Unknown current restrictions, live depth, order terms, exact customs exposure, project-level returns and target-company eliminations are explicitly retained.

The principal open questions are whether stock and receivables reconcile to cash, whether IPO and related-party governance remediation is complete, how much group cash is legally usable at each entity, when borrowings mature and can be renewed, whether the recent packaging ramp earns adequate returns after full capital needs, and what the effective merger would do to each shareholder's economic interest. Until these are answered, a supported base IRR, normalized owner-PAT forecast and ordinary investment score remain NS.

The reproducible record separates authored inputs from generated outputs. Its aggregate authored-input fingerprint binds an ordered list of input names and SHA256 values; it is **not the SHA256 file hash of the report or reader record**. Those file hashes are separately attested after generation. The recovery test starts with every generated output and attestation poisoned or deleted, disallows network and subprocess use, permits only declared authored input reads or outputs written during that run, and performs verification inside those guards. This protects reproducibility, not the truth of a management forecast. Research update: first full v3.0 assessment at the stated cutoff; no prior company score is silently overwritten.
